source.title: Train the Model, Not the Reader: Decodability Supervision for Verifiable Activation Explanations

record.tranche_reason: The study audits activation explanations using claim flips and exact synthetic ground truth, rather than measuring neuron poles or applying the neuron-explanation evaluation described in the claim versions. Its results conceptually test whether reconstruction-scored explanations are faithful.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on activation verbalizers and reconstruction scores, not on the share of neurons or neuron poles with named jobs. It does not test neuron-level explanations on held-out activating examples as specified in V6 or report a neuron-level score distribution as specified in V7. Rows linked to V7 concern claim-level faithfulness of NLA explanations, not the version's exact neuron-level measure. Cited findings from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study audits natural-language autoencoder explanations of whole residual-stream activations, which are scored by reconstructing the activation. It does not explain or score individual neurons or neuron poles. It also does not simulate neuron activations on new text or count shares of interpretable units. The scoring method differs from V7's, which simulates activations, and the unit explained differs too: whole activation vectors rather than neurons. So no row measures what any version names. Neuron explanations appear only in related work (a cite of Huang et al. 2023). The claim-level faithfulness findings are a related but different construct and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. Two additions: training the reader toward grounding (RAFT/GRPO) or toward reconstruction similarity fails, through proxy gaming and representation collapse. And a RECAP probe still flags score-gaming lies (AUC 0.95 vs 0.51 control), so the reconstruction score should not be used as a truth signal.
record.recipe_differences: The study audits natural-language autoencoder reconstruction using claim-level flips and synthetic ground truth; it does not conduct a neuron-pole interpretability audit. The released Qwen NLA recipe is used for some experiments, but the study's audit method and target claim differ from the original neuron-pole claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Grounding fraction varies with flip threshold (τ=0.02, 0.05, 0.10). In the sandbox, grounding on code-bearing slots depends on using the co-trained versus independent evaluator. The study also reports variation across scenario, seed, target design, and RECAP settings.

fits_no_version.finding: On the released Qwen-2.5-7B layer-20 NLA, reconstruction is r̃=0.84, yet only 4.2%/2.1%/1.6% of salient specific claims are flip-grounded. The score survives paraphrase (0.89 kept) but collapses when content words are masked (0.04 kept).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reconstruction-scored activation explanations can score highly by gist while their specific claims are largely ungrounded.

fits_no_version.finding: In the synthetic sandbox, standard co-trained NLA pairs develop grounded-but-false private codes in 5/5 runs, with grounded-minus-true gaps of 0.30–0.80. Under an independent evaluator, grounding on code-bearing slots collapses from 0.53–0.89 to 0.08–0.23.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Co-trained verbalizer/reconstructor pairs can pass reconstruction tests via pair-specific false wording.

fits_no_version.finding: RECAP decodability supervision of the target model removes codes in the sandbox. On Pythia-160M it raises verbalizer truth from 0.06 to 0.44 and probe AUC for ranking true over false claims from 0.823 to 0.965. Verbalizers still convey only part of the decodable content.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training target models to keep designated content decodable makes activation explanations checkable by probes, though not fully verbalizable.

record.problems: The authors state that evidence covers one released NLA, a synthetic sandbox, and continued pretraining of one small model; most experiments use single seeds. The audits cover closed-vocabulary claims, and RECAP covers only designated content. The Qwen grounding fractions are explicitly sensitivity-limited lower bounds.
record.rows_left_out: Other measurements about probe drift, representation collapse, language-modeling tax, and adversarial monitoring were not included because they do not directly measure activation-explanation claim faithfulness or neuron interpretability for these versions.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or job shares.
No comparison of interpretable-neuron share across architectures or tools.
No neuron-based attribution graphs. It only notes that a patched tap barely moves behaviour (~0.003), which concerns RECAP content, not circuits.
No neuron explanations checked against where neurons fire.
No neuron explanations scored by simulating activations on new text, and no share of well-scored neurons.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked rows to V7 by analogy: unfaithful explanations scored by an automated metric. V7, however, concerns neuron explanations scored by activation simulation, which this study never measures. All rows are therefore relinked to none and no verdicts are given. The study is not one of the originals.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit, neuron-pole counts, or shares of poles with one or two jobs or unknown jobs.
No cross-model or model-scale comparison of neuron-pole interpretability.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car example or test of recursive generalization versus superposition.
No comparison of architecture, regularization, or tools for neuron interpretability, and no InceptionV1-sized vision-model estimates.
No attribution-graph test of whether model neurons suffice as circuit units. The paper notes that designated content can be behaviorally inert, but does not test attribution graphs.
The study does not test explanations against where neurons fire on new examples; it audits claims about activation content.
Tests claim-level faithfulness of reconstruction-scored activation explanations, not the fraction of individual neuron explanations receiving good scores on new text.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Claim-level audits of the released Qwen-2.5-7B NLA and standard synthetic NLA runs
reader_labels.reason: Only 1.6–4.2% of Qwen salient specific claims met the flip-grounding thresholds, and standard sandbox runs produced grounded false wording; these results support the claim-level challenge to relying on reconstruction scoring as a faithfulness signal (r1–r3, r11).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: With designated content trained to remain decodable, fresh verbalizers were approximately 1.00 truthful and grounded and codes were not observed; the poor-faithfulness results do not apply uniformly to this intervention (r14).
